steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes and cook until tender but still firm, about 15 minutes; drain and chop.

At the same time, place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring water to a boil; cover, remove from heat, and let eggs stand in hot water for 10 to 12 minutes. Remove from hot water; peel and chop.
Combine cooked and chopped potatoes and eggs with mayonnaise, celery, relish, garlic, mustard, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Gently mix together and serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern Potato Salad
raw_recipe.description: This Southern potato salad with warm potatoes, hard boiled eggs, crunchy celery, mayo, sweet pickle, and mustard is creamy, tangy, and delicious.
raw_recipe.name: Southern Potato Salad

review.reviewBody: I have made potato salad like this all my 50 years of cooking as my mother and grandmother before me. Must be a southern recipe only. I add just about l tblsp. cider vinegar and a tblspn of sugar when mixing. Seems to improve the flavor. Garnish top with sliced boiled eggs sprinkled with paparika. All the northerners in my family request this dish for all family get to gathers.

This potato salad was a good basic start - but to be really 'Southern' it needs some Bacon! I fry mine up while the potatoes/eggs are boiling. I pour some hot bacon geese on my drained potatoes and let them 'soak it up' for a delicious Bacon flavor throughout. Here's a few tips: 1. To save on pots, use only 1 pot to boil first the quartered Red or Golden Potatoes w/skins and later toss in the eggs the last 10 mins. or so. 2. A friend of mine used to use 'Green Onion Ends' and they really added a nice taste. 3. Like others have advised, mix up your sauce separately -- to taste. A little bit of milk smooths it out. 4. There are 2 types of tastes = Sweet or Sour. Sweet = Chopped Bread & Butter Pickles w/juice. NO mustard. Use Apple Cedar Vinegar instead. Sour = Chopped Dill Pickles or Dill Weed. Mustard. 5. Parsley and chopped black olives take it up a notch, too! I've been making it for decades and everyone raves about it! Enjoy!

My recipe almost and let me add that most southern cooks do not use sweet relish in mustard style potato salad but instead use dill pickles chopped. So omit sweet relish and use Mt. Olive zesty garlic kosher dill spears; also I finely chop about a fourth of a green bell pepper and omit the garlic and add a medium sized onion, chopped. Does not matter on white or yellow onion and you might even want to try a Vidalia sometime. One other thing, we never serve this style of potato salad warm, always serve it cold. Try this way, you might like it even more. Personally I have never liked mine warm unless I’m making a version of German style potato salad. One other note here, add some paprika mixed in and sprinkle to your taste over the top before you serve it. I read in the reviews one thing that can be absolutely true when it comes to making potato salad, one time you can make it and it is perfect and yet you can do it on another day using same ingredients and it just refuses to taste the same. Don’t know if it is the potato or the egg or what it is but this is a definite you can count on.

I loved the review by the lady who is 70 and been making potato salad for decades. Ditto..almost 70 myself, southern all the way. I detest dill so have always used sweet relish, black olives, pimento, mayo and mustard mixed, boiled eggs (I boil them on topp of the potatoes) sauteed onions and celery (yep, I saute' them), occasionally garlic powder or salt, season all, paprika, pepper.. And I've even added baby shrimp or tuna.. I definitely chill it before eating if there's time, but it's always better the next day--great w/saltine crackers. It's all about your own individual taste. A lot of these recipes are a foundation for us to use if we don't know how to make it. But any good cook tweaks a recipe for personal taste. I can't think of one recipe I've ever followed to the letter. My dad was a military chef who worked for generals and started teaching me how to cook when I was 9 years old. Love making people happy with recipes they enjoy. :-) Allrecipes has some amazing recipes and terrific ideas.

Good base recipe to make as-is or to tweak to your liking. I poured a little apple cider vinegar over the potatoes after cooking/chopping but before adding the rest of the dressing and let it soak that in while cooling, and also added paprika, fresh dill, and cucumber to the dish. Turned out exactly as I expected and wanted it to.

Right off the bat, for flavor enhancement --and to protect stomachs sensitive to raw onions: I "carmelized" the onions (red and also 'sweet' onions). Also, I used Trader's aioli mustard.== for me, this recipe uses too much mustard)... --- For color & taste, I use green onion tops and shaved carrot, slightly browned/carmelized in iron skillet-- THEN all was topped with fresh dill and cherry tomatoes. yummm. PS: DEFINITELY, I recommend cooking the eggs 'til they're actually boiled all the way thru.

Excellent potato salad! I did things differently. I peeled and chopped the potatoes before boiling them. They were ready in just over 10 min. I've made potato salad that's been flavorless, so while the potatoes were still warm, I sprinkled about a tblsp of Greek salad dressing over and let soak in. At this time, I also followed what a reviewer who knows about Southern cooking mentioned and that was adding apple cider vinegar and a little sugar. Adding the dressing and vinegar were probably what made this a little mushy, but I didn't care.....it was so delicious! I also did not miss the onions. While serving, I like to also top with some green olives or radishes. Thanks for this great recipe which I'll surely make again!

My mothers family were Germans that migrated to southern Appalachia in the 1800's. They had been miners in Germany and went to work in the mines here. In the early 1900's they moved to Zeigler Ill., to work in the coal mines there. Her potato had been handed down through the generations. Yours is very close. She used white potatoes, because that is what Dad could grow in the garden, She used sweet pickles that she diced holding the bowl in her lap. Used a half a onion, full stalk of celery, but never any garlic. The one thing that she did, that II haven't seen in any of the recipe sites that I visit, she would mash an egg yoke, to which she added the Mayo and mustard, that gets that great yoke flavor across all of the salad.

I’ve made Southern potato salad all my life and get many raves. I don’t use garlic. I use dill relish. Mostly don’t use mustard, but can. I add green onions. I salt heavily with Himalayan or sea salt and Russet potatoes. After boiling, skinning, and chopping potatoes, I put the onion, salt, pepper, and relish in refrigerator for overnight while warm. Next day add celery, eggs, and lastly mayonnaise. Chill and eat next day. Only for a sweeter salad use sweet relish and Mayo or Miracle Whip (some people like it).

Very easy but full of flavor! I agree with adding vinegar and a pinch of sugar to balance the acid. I also added Sicilian Oregano, smoked paprika, pinch of cayenne pepper, & pepperoncini. An elevated flavor with a slight kick in every bite!

I added a bit of paprika at the end for more of a garnish. While the potatoes were still warm I added a small amount (1 1/2 tablespoons) of white wine vinegar for a small bite and (1 tablespoon) of regular white sugar for mellowness. Turned out great. Thank you!!!

I absolutely love this recipe! I made a couple tweaks to it. I took some of my fresh refrigerator pickles I made and chopped them up and added them with the relish, I used red onion and garlic powder instead of fresh garlic but I will try fresh garlic next time. My husband is not crazy about regular potato salad, but this recipe changed his mind! He said it’s the best he has ever had and he said he could eat it warm or cold and I was floored! I never thought I would ever hear him say that! It’s just the two of us in the house now and when I went to put the leftovers away, there was only enough potato salad left for one serving! I had two servings, so he ate the rest!! Wow, what an amazing recipe! Thanks for sharing!
Loved this recipe
I added sweet onions and red bell peppers. Skipped the garlic.
What I liked about this recipe is that it's a small portion, and it gets you right in the ballpark.
So good
My potatoes came out too crunchy

It was the first time I actually made potato salad and it came out great. I used a combination of yellow and red potatoes and made the 4 serving option. Next time I might add more celery. If you like celery you may want to increase it to one stalk. I made it exactly as recommended since it was my first time. The only swap I made was LITE mayonnaise instead of the regular. Very easy to follow for a beginner.
This is a delicious basic potato salad recipe that we've made over and over again, still not tired of it!
One stalk is the whole bunch of celery, I think you mean one rib of celery which is one piece.
